questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you do not see any other cars.
Signal only if you see other cars.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you do not see any other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you turn, change lanes, or pull away from the curb. Do not skip this step. Make it a habit to always signal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for you, so you must wait for them to pass before you cross.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Do not make any driving errors.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at or near the accident scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: You must stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand in traffic lanes—another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving the same way as:
questions.explanation: Being tired and drinking alcohol have the same effect on your driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs you like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, or cross multiple lanes suddenly on the highway. Do not cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of using a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally or in the wrong place. Always protect pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what to do. It means you should keep right to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the situation. Always drive at or below the speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas in your vision that appear when you get tired.
Areas of the road you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go. Check near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them to you.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave to the driver first.
Only if pedestrians are not texting while walking.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian or vehicle cross. You can carefully move forward only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more distance between your vehicle and the ones ahead.

questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the space between your vehicle and others because slippery roads require more distance to stop.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps you drive safely?

options.text: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid impaired driving is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee or cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level. Your body needs about one hour to eliminate alcohol from one drink.

questions.question: Since driving involves risk, it is smart to keep improving your driving and observation skills.
questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe when drivers think they have nothing left to learn. For your safety and others' safety, always work to improve your driving and observation skills.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals when you move left or right. Use your signal when entering traffic from a parking space, moving to a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: In the District of Columbia, your driver license can be revoked if you are convicted of a drug offense, even if it is not driving-related.
questions.explanation: Your driver license can be revoked in the District of Columbia if you are convicted of a drug offense, even if it is not driving-related.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal in advance, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Stops the seat belt warning light or buzzer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge in.
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign tells you that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working when you drive.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving ability. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, and sadness all make it harder to concentrate. Wait to drive until you feel calm and stable.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see ahead clearly, at an intersection, near a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no passing zone. Never pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: Your vision is limited at night. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: On a freeway, you miss your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Turn quickly from your current lane.
Keep driving until the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder. It is illegal.
